title: O A T P one B one and simvastatin

segs.text: Section seventeen. O A T P one B one and simvastatin. O A T P one B one is the second transporter she covered, and a newer one than P glycoprotein. The gene is S L C O one B one, and the protein is O A T P one B one. It sits in the liver, on the hepatocyte sinusoidal membrane, not in the gut. It handles hepatic uptake of weakly acidic drugs and endogenous compounds, such as statins, methotrexate and bilirubin. At least forty non synonymous S N Ps are known.

Star five is one S N P, r s four one four nine zero five six, which is five twenty one T to C, valine one seventy four to alanine. It has reduced function, possibly from reduced expression, and it is rare, about one percent. Star fifteen and star seventeen are the common ones, five to fifteen percent in European and Asian populations. They are haplotypes that contain the star five S N P plus other S N Ps. She said, Remember, these two are haplotypes, which means they contain more than one snip. So any two of these alleles give two copies of the star five S N P, and count as homozygous.

O A T P one B one takes simvastatin into the liver. A reduced function transporter takes up less, so more simvastatin stays in the plasma. Patients homozygous for the star five S N P have a large increase in simvastatin plasma exposure, measured as area under the curve. The increase is two hundred twenty one percent, which she read aloud as two hundred twenty one times. Either way, the increase is large.

High statin levels cause muscle breakdown, and pain in the large muscles is the warning symptom. In rhabdomyolysis, the contents of the muscle cells enter the blood and damage the kidneys. That is why patients are now often genotyped for star five, fifteen and seventeen. For at least one nonfunctional allele, lower the simvastatin dose or give another statin. She said some other statins cause less rhabdomyolysis, so a different statin may be better than just a lower dose.
